how: The member who proposes the picture also maps its squares and calls others to help build it.
Repeated calls recruit members to build and finish specific parts of the shared picture.
A newcomer requests orientation and receives the pixel interval and an explanation of the shared defence effort.
A member answers the removal-script proposal with an unqualified twelve-hour running commitment.
Members propose the room's picture, plan expansion, and ask where its name should go.
Reports of the hat finished and the picture half done expose the state of construction to other readers.
Coordinates locate the proposed work and a mapped blueprint prescribes its individual squares.
Building requires requesting and opening a coordination channel as well as posting the state of the work.
Members direct participants to chat for orders and return changed plans to readers outside that chat.
Changing the picture includes circulating the replacement decision beyond the chat so people outside it can follow the new plan.
A blueprint and advertised orders neither test an aggregate frequency claim nor disclose whether formal leaders or sanctions were decided inside the unseen chat.
Participants share a placement bot, offer a removal script, commit to running it, and report success.
Members repeatedly rally to guard their picture, repair changed messages, and stand ground against reported attacks.
A withdrawn accusation and an explanation of the allied border separate mistaken blame from an actual hostile incursion.
A construction report identifies aligned builders unknowingly overwriting the shared picture rather than assigning all interference to enemies.
Members propose a border that accommodates another flag and explain where their work stops at an allied boundary.
A direct answer spares the rainbow on grounds of non-aggression and its protection of the yellow buildup.
Participants report outside reinforcements and thank an ally for substantial help.
A named multi-group alliance invitation and reports of friendly neighbours make coalition membership visible.
A member reports asking another subreddit to guard the work, supporting a representative act without establishing appointment to an office.
The allied border explanation establishes neighbouring work but does not establish host authority over a guest's construction.
Correcting an accusation against an ally supplies no observed dispute over who may commit the room to agreements.
Homesteading calls and an appeal to cover a communist area direct placers against selected rivals' work.
A final-result assessment compares the intact helicopter favourably against the ideological rival's mark.
A defender is encouraged to continue because the room is outnumbered.
The replacement helicopter plan does not state that loss or overrunning prompted relocation.
Participants celebrate the unvandalized final helicopter and praise those who made it.
The final-result assessment records how the work survived in the same passage that celebrates it.
A post invites friends to a replica drawing and a reply acknowledges discovering the successor venue.
An invitation and acknowledgement warrant continuation as a proposal without warranting a collective move or completed successor drawing.
The final-result assessment reports survival without an observed dispute over cleaning a copy or correcting the event's history.
Members reveal an April Fools punchline and extend jokes about whether physical removal lasts beyond that day.
The joke frame applies to identified local performances rather than automatically cancelling practical canvas calls and blueprints.
A member evaluates the canvas's worth and advises brief enjoyment followed by moving on.
Referring defenders to a canvas subreddit establishes routing without establishing that the host opened it or imposed a posting boundary.
The proposed picture brings the room's political jokes into the canvas through its named character and emblem.
A familiar ideological enemy is named in calls to overwrite its flags rather than being invented solely from neighbouring pixels.
The attack call names communist enemies and ANTICOM yellow in the same turn.
A participant celebrates month-long subreddit growth without naming canvas exposure as its cause.

statement: distinguishing growth pride from canvas recruitment
how: Month-long growth pride does not establish whether encountering the canvas mark brought new members into the room.
The invasion report remains political venue talk whose quoted text alone does not establish canvas conduct.

statement: seeking a more exclusionary political venue
how: The wish for a more exclusionary political venue does not itself describe pixel work or canvas coordination.
A member starts by proposing the picture and calling for helpers in the same turn, then supplies its mapped blueprint.
The initiating thread proceeds from a build call to progress reports without establishing which individual placers the call recruited.
A prescribed blueprint follows the proposal without an observed design argument whose settlement could test the theorised mechanism.
A removal-script proposal receives a bare running commitment, supporting this local answer without establishing the general preference mechanism or silent placing.
Placed parts already need damage control while the larger picture remains under construction.
Defence calls and a later border explanation coexist without a cited passage establishing that erosion caused the negotiation.
The rainbow refusal cites a norm and protective benefit without disclosing a prior negotiated agreement that could test treaty-induced restraint.
The script explicitly erases a rival mark, but neither that goal nor its running commitment establishes maintenance pressure as the cause of automation.
The same passage reports attack and requests outside guards, linking defence pressure to seeking additional hands.
The border explanation and thanks for help do not disclose whether border negotiation opened the channel through which help arrived.
Attack reports and coalition recruitment establish joint presence without disclosing why or when the alliance was formed.
Mobilization begins with calls to overwrite ideological enemies before the room's specific picture is proposed.
A question proposing to cover the rainbow receives a reasoned refusal, while another branch redirects expansion against an ideological enemy.
An expansion accusation receives a border-and-alliance explanation, although the unavailable edit time prevents attributing the retraction to that reply.
Attack proposals and later comparative victory talk do not themselves establish that the former caused the latter.
Being outnumbered does not suffice to explain withdrawal when members continue requesting protection and later call for standing ground.
Construction reports precede final celebration, but that sequence alone cannot establish how a finished mark prompted the room's pride.
A final-result passage both records survival and celebrates it, so celebration and recording need not occupy separate ordered stages.
The later replica invitation does not identify the earlier final-result account as its reason for continuing.
Calls and defence referrals do not establish a canvas-post flood or a boundary rule adopted because of it.
An accusation corrected through an alliance explanation does not test whether agreements generate disputes over authority to bind members.
A removal script and a commitment to run it connect machine-assisted placing to the explicit goal of erasing a rival's mark.
